steps.say: A seed holds a tiny plant and a store of food. When it starts to grow, we call it germination.

figure.alt: A seed grows into a seedling, then into a plant.

steps.say: Most seeds need water, warmth and air to germinate. They do not need light yet.
First a root grows down. Then a shoot grows up towards the light.
When the stored food runs out, the leaves must make food. Now the plant needs light.
To grow well, plants need light, water, air, warmth and minerals from the soil.
Plants grow towards light. Without light, they grow pale, thin and weak.

check.prompt: Which of these do most seeds need to germinate?

options.why: Most seeds germinate in the dark.
Seeds can germinate on wet cotton wool.
Cold slows seeds down. They need warmth.

hints: Think of seeds sprouting in a warm, dark cupboard.
Seeds need three things, and one of them is water.
Cross out anything a seed on wet cotton wool would not have.
check.explanation: Most seeds need water, warmth and air to germinate. Light and soil are not needed at the start.

check.prompt: When a seed starts to grow, it is called ___.
hints: It is a science word you met in this lesson.
It starts with the letter g.
check.explanation: Germination is when a seed starts to grow.
